mainTopic: Annulling a נדר על דעת רבים, the end of מומין אלו, and the new משנה on the two kinds of בכור (inheritance and כהן)
overview: This עמוד finishes פרק מומין אלו and opens a new פרק about the בכור. First, a כהן who married a woman forbidden to him is made to vow על דעת רבים. אמימר rules that such a vow cannot be annulled, but the גמרא adds that it can be annulled for a דבר מצוה. A story about רבינא bringing back an excellent teacher of children shows this exception. Next, the גמרא explains why a כהן who became טמא למתים needs only a קבלה: in the marriage case, his יצר is strong. After the הדרן, the new משנה teaches that 'בכור' is two separate laws. Inheritance follows the father's first son, and פדיון from the כהן follows the mother's first birth. It lists cases of a בכור for inheritance only, including a dispute between רבי מאיר and חכמים and a dispute with רבי יוסי הגלילי. It then lists cases of a בכור for the כהן only, such as mixed-up babies and a widow who remarried too soon.

steps.title: The vow is administered based on public consent
steps.stepSummary: The end of the previous sentence: we make the כהן vow על דעת רבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [We make him vow] based on the consent of the public.
steps.whatsHappening: This עמוד begins in the middle of a sentence from the previous דף. It finishes the statement that the כהן who married a forbidden woman is made to vow על דעת רבים, which means his vow is tied to the public's consent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying a vow to the public's consent makes it much harder to undo, because a חכם cannot simply release it. This is how the vow is made strong enough to really keep the כהן away from the forbidden woman. The next step explains the legal power of this kind of vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Based on the consent of the public; a vow tied to the public's will
We administer a vow (we make him vow)

phrases.english: [we make] him [vow] based on the consent of the public.
phrases.notes: Continuation of a sentence from the previous דף: ומדרינן ליה אדעת רבים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement that began on the previous דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן who married a forbidden woman is made to vow על דעת רבים.

steps.title: A vow based on public consent cannot be annulled
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that a vow made על דעת רבים has no הפרה, even according to the view that a vow made in public does.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: The הלכה is that even according to the one who says a vow made in public can be annulled, a vow made based on the consent of the public cannot be annulled.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר gives the final הלכה about how strong a vow על דעת רבים is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different things here. A vow made in front of many people (ברבים) is one level, and some hold it can still be annulled. A vow made על דעת רבים depends on the public's consent, so all agree it cannot be annulled without them.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha is; the final ruling
A vow made in the presence of the public
Annulment of a vow
According to the one who says

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'ברבים' (in public, in front of people) with 'על דעת רבים' (dependent on the public's consent). The first is weaker. The second is the strong one that cannot be annulled.

phrases.english: Ameimar said: The halakha is:
even according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: נֶדֶר שֶׁהוּדַּר בָּרַבִּים יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה,
phrases.english: a vow that was made in public has annulment,

phrases.aramaic: עַל דַּעַת הָרַבִּים אֵין לוֹ הֲפָרָה.
phrases.english: [one made] on the consent of the public has no annulment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the legal strength of the vow על דעת רבים mentioned in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדר על דעת רבים cannot be annulled, according to all opinions.

steps.title: Exception: annulment for the sake of a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only to a דבר הרשות. For a דבר מצוה, even a vow על דעת רבים can be annulled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to an optional matter. But for a matter of a מצוה, it can be annulled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits אמימר's rule by adding an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strong vow stays locked only when the reason to undo it is a personal, optional matter. If annulling it would allow a מצוה to happen, it can be annulled. The general category of a vow על דעת רבים stays the same. Only the outcome changes in this exceptional case.

keyTerms.meaning: And this matter applies [only]; introduces a limitation
An optional matter
A matter of a מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the practical guideline: a vow על דעת רבים may be undone when it stands in the way of a מצוה.

phrases.english: And this applies to an optional matter,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה.
phrases.english: but for a matter of a מצוה it has annulment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of אמימר's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדר על דעת רבים can be annulled when this is needed for a דבר מצוה.

steps.title: The story of the children's teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא made a negligent teacher vow (על דעת רבים) to stop teaching. רבינא annulled the vow and brought him back, because no one else was as careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: As in the case of a certain teacher of young children. רב אחא made him vow [to stop teaching] because he was negligent with the children. And רבינא brought him back, because they did not find anyone who was as careful as he was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case to show the מצוה exception in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching Torah to children is a מצוה. So even though the teacher's vow was tied to public consent, רבינא annulled it and brought him back. No other teacher was as precise in his teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Who teaches young children (to read)
He made him vow
Was negligent with the children (e.g., hit them too much)
He brought him back / reinstated him
Careful, precise

steps.whatToRemember: A vow על דעת רבים cannot normally be annulled, but it can be undone for a מצוה. The example is bringing back an excellent teacher of children.

phrases.english: As that one who taught young children,
Rav Aḥa made him vow [to stop teaching]
because he was negligent with the children,
and Ravina reinstated him,
because he did not find anyone who was as meticulous as him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the מצוה exception from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That a נדר על דעת רבים may be annulled for a דבר מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבינא annulled the vow and reinstated the teacher, since teaching children is a מצוה and no one was as careful.

steps.title: Why a commitment for impurity but a vow for marriage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a כהן who became טמא למתים. It asks why he only needs a קבלה, while a כהן who married a forbidden woman needs a נדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who becomes impure to the dead, etc.' What is different here, that a commitment is enough for him? And what is different there, that we make him vow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks why the two cases are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both כהנים did a forbidden act and are disqualified until they show they have stopped. The טמא למתים only needs to accept upon himself not to repeat it. The one who married a forbidden woman must take a formal vow. The question is what justifies this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: One (a כהן) who becomes impure through the dead
What is the difference
It is enough for him
Accepting a commitment (without a formal vow)

phrases.english: 'And one who becomes impure to the dead, etc.'
What is different here
that acceptance is enough for him,
and what is different there
that we make him vow?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּסַגִּי לֵיהּ בְּקַבָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a נדר is required for forbidden marriage but only a קבלה for טומאת מת.

steps.title: Desire overpowers him there
steps.stepSummary: In the marriage case, the כהן's desire is strong, so a firmer safeguard (a vow) is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the marriage case involves strong desire, so a simple commitment is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Becoming impure is not driven by an ongoing craving, so a simple commitment can be trusted. Attraction to a woman is a powerful יצר that can easily break a simple promise. A binding vow is therefore needed.

keyTerms.meaning: His desire (inclination) overpowers him

steps.whatToRemember: How strong a safeguard must be depends on how strong the temptation is. A vow is needed for marriage because of the יצר. A commitment is enough for טומאה.

phrases.english: There, his desire seizes him.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the marriage case, the כהן's יצר is strong, so a vow is required. With טומאה, there is no such pull.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק מומין אלו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק מומין אלו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק 'מומין אלו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the פרק with the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is not a legal argument. It marks the end of the פרק, and the next פרק begins afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (closing formula of a perek)
'These blemishes', the name of the perek

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'These Blemishes'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final discussion.

steps.title: Four kinds of firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה states that a son can be a בכור for inheritance only, for the כהן only, for both, or for neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a son who is a firstborn for inheritance but not a firstborn for the כהן. There is one who is a firstborn for the כהן but not for inheritance. There is one who is a firstborn for both. And there is one who is not a firstborn for either.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins. The משנה sets up a framework of four categories that it will explain one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is that 'בכור' is really two separate laws. בכור לנחלה depends on the FATHER: it is his first son, and that son gets a double portion. בכור לכהן depends on the MOTHER: it is the first baby to open her womb, and he needs פדיון הבן. Since these follow different people, they can split apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
Firstborn for inheritance. This is the father's first son, who gets a double portion.
Firstborn for the כהן. This is the mother's first birth, and he must be redeemed with five סלעים.
'Opener of the womb.' This is the first baby out of the mother.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'firstborn' means just one thing. Inheritance follows the father, and redemption follows the mother. Almost every case in this פרק depends on keeping these two apart.
steps.whyThisMatters: This four-way chart is the map for the whole פרק. Each case that follows fits into one of these boxes.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
There is a firstborn for inheritance,
who is not a firstborn for the priest;
a firstborn for the priest who is not a firstborn for inheritance;
a firstborn for both inheritance and the priest,
and there is one who is not a firstborn
neither for inheritance nor for the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ יֵשׁ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְאֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new פרק after the הדרן of מומין אלו in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two independent kinds of בכור, inheritance and כהן, which give four possible combinations.

steps.title: Born after a miscarriage or stillbirth: inheritance yes, כהן no
steps.stepSummary: A son born after a נפל, a stillborn full-term baby, or an animal-shaped miscarriage inherits as a בכור but is not redeemed. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which son is a firstborn for inheritance but not for the כהן? One who comes after miscarried non-viable babies, even if the miscarried baby's head came out alive. Or one who comes after a full nine-month baby whose head came out dead. Or one born to a woman who had miscarried something shaped like a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now explains the first of its four categories and gives concrete cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case something already came out of the mother's womb, so the next son is not the פטר רחם and needs no פדיון. But the earlier birth was not a living, viable son of the father. So the next son is still the father's first real son and gets the double inheritance. רבי מאיר holds that even an animal-shaped miscarriage counts as opening the womb.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-viable babies (miscarriages) that cannot survive
A full-term, nine-month baby
A woman who miscarries
The תנא whose view this is

steps.confusionAlert: 'Even if its head came out alive' describes the נפל, not the son we are discussing. Even a נפל that came out partly alive does not take away the next son's inheritance rights. It does, however, open the womb.

phrases.english: Which is a firstborn for inheritance
but not a firstborn for the priest?
One who comes after miscarried non-viable fetuses,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיָּצָא אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ חַי,
phrases.english: even though its head came out alive,
or a nine-month baby whose head came out dead,
or a woman who miscarries something like a domestic animal, wild animal, or bird —
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזֶהוּ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְאֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first category listed in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any earlier birth from the womb, even a non-viable one or an animal-shaped one (according to רבי מאיר), takes away the כהן status but not the inheritance status.

steps.title: חכמים: only a human-shaped miscarriage counts
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. An earlier miscarriage only opens the womb if it had some human form.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: it does not count until it has some form of a human being.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give a dissenting opinion on the animal-shaped miscarriage from step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said that an animal-shaped miscarriage opens the womb. The חכמים require some human form. Without it, the miscarriage does not count as a birth, so the next son is still the פטר רחם and does need פדיון.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view
Human form or shape

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
not unless it has something of a human form.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ מִצּוּרַת אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר's last case in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a miscarriage with some human form opens the womb.

steps.title: More cases that open the womb
steps.stepSummary: A son who comes after a סנדל, a שליא, a developed שפיר, or a baby delivered in pieces is a בכור for inheritance but not for the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a woman miscarries a sandal-shaped fetus, or an afterbirth, or a sac with formed tissue, or a baby that came out in pieces, then the son born after these is a firstborn for inheritance but not a firstborn for the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds more types of earlier births that already opened the womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these is an abnormal or non-viable birth. It is enough to count as opening the womb, so the next son needs no פדיון. None of them was a living son of the father, so the next son still inherits the double portion.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat, sandal-shaped fetus (thought of like a sandal fish)
Afterbirth or placenta
A gestational sac with formed tissue
Cut up, delivered in pieces

phrases.english: A woman who miscarries a sandal-fetus, or an afterbirth,
or a sac with developed tissue,
or one that emerges in pieces —
the one who comes after them is a firstborn for inheritance,
but not a firstborn for the priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of cases for the first category.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Abnormal births like a סנדל, שליא, שפיר מרוקם, or a baby in pieces open the womb.

steps.title: A mother who already gave birth before
steps.stepSummary: If a man with no sons marries a woman who already had a child, even as a שפחה or a נכרית, their son inherits as a בכור but is not redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man who had no sons married a woman who had already given birth. Or she had given birth while still a שפחה and was later freed. Or she had given birth while still a נכרית and later converted. If she then gave birth after joining Israel, that son is a firstborn for inheritance but not a firstborn for the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a different kind of case. Here the split comes from the mother's earlier children, not from a miscarriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son is his father's first son, so he gets the double inheritance. But the mother's womb was already opened by an earlier baby, so he is not a פטר רחם. This holds even if the earlier birth happened before she was a free Jewish woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A Canaanite maidservant
She was freed
A non-Jewish woman
She converted

steps.whatToRemember: Inheritance follows the father's first son. Redemption follows the mother's first birth. According to the תנא קמא, any earlier birth from the mother, even before she was freed or converted, cancels פדיון for later sons. רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees in the next step.

phrases.english: One who had no sons,
and married a woman who had already given birth,
or she gave birth while still a maidservant and was then freed,
or while still a gentile and then converted,
and after she came into Israel she gave birth —
he is a firstborn for inheritance but not a firstborn for the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים וְנָשָׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁכְּבָר יָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new type of case to the first category, based on the mother's earlier births.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mother's earlier birth, even before she was freed or converted, takes away כהן status from later sons, but the father's first son still inherits as a בכור.

steps.title: A birth before becoming Jewish does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees with the previous case. A child born to a woman who earlier gave birth as a נכרית or שפחה is a בכור for both inheritance and the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: he is a בכור for inheritance and for the כהן. The verse says 'פטר רחם בישראל,' meaning the womb must be opened among Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי argues on the case just taught, where the mother had a child earlier as a שפחה or נכרית. He says the son she has now is a full בכור in every way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said the earlier non-Jewish birth already 'opened the womb,' so this son is not redeemed. רבי יוסי הגלילי reads 'בישראל' to mean only a womb opened while the mother was Jewish counts. So the earlier birth is ignored, and this son is the first to open the womb as a Jewish birth.

keyTerms.meaning: Opening of the womb, meaning the first birth from the mother
Among the Jewish people
Inheritance (the בכור gets a double portion)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
He is a firstborn for inheritance and for the priest,
as it is stated: 'Opening the womb among Israel' —
meaning only once they open a womb as part of Israel.
phrases.notes: A womb opened while the mother was not Jewish does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Dissents from the ruling in Step 12 about a mother who gave birth earlier as a שפחה or נכרית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A birth before the mother became Jewish does not open the womb halachically, so the next son is a בכור for both inheritance and the כהן.

steps.title: Second category begins: a firstborn of the mother but not of the father
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens the list of cases where the son is a בכור for the כהן but not for inheritance. These are: a man who already had sons, a mother who converted while pregnant, and a mother who was freed from slavery while pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who already had sons and married a woman who had never given birth. Or a woman who converted while pregnant. Or a woman who was freed while pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins listing cases for its second category. The ruling for all of them ('בכור לכהן ואינו בכור לנחלה') comes only at the end of the list, in Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the baby is the first to open his mother's womb, so he must be redeemed from the כהן. But he is not his father's firstborn. Either the father already had sons, or halachically the baby has no father: a convert's or freed slave's child conceived before her change of status has no legal יחוס to that father. Inheritance follows the father, so there is no double portion.

keyTerms.meaning: She converted
Pregnant
She was freed (from being a שפחה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 12. There the father had no sons and the mother had given birth before (בכור for inheritance only). Here it is the reverse: the mother never gave birth, but the father is not counted (בכור for the כהן only).

phrases.english: One who had sons
and married a woman who had not given birth;
a woman who converted while pregnant;
a maidservant who was freed while pregnant.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים וְנָשָׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁלֹּא יָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'inheritance only' category to the second category listed in Step 8: 'for the כהן only.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the son opens his mother's womb but is not his father's legal firstborn, he is redeemed but gets no double portion.

steps.title: Babies mixed up between two mothers
steps.stepSummary: The list continues with mix-up cases. An Israelite woman gave birth at the same time as a כהנת, a לויה, or a woman who had already given birth, and the babies got mixed up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she (an Israelite woman) gave birth along with a כהנת, or a לויה, or a woman who had already given birth, and it is unknown which baby belongs to which mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds more cases to the same list. These are cases where two babies were born together and got mixed up, so nobody knows whose son is whose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child of a כהנת or a לויה is never redeemed, and neither is a child of a woman who already gave birth. So when one of these babies is mixed up with an Israelite's first child, it is unclear which baby needs פדיון. Since no father can identify his own son, neither baby can claim a firstborn's double portion. How the פדיון payment works with this doubt is discussed later in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman of priestly family (daughter or wife of a כהן)
A woman of Levite family
Who had already given birth

phrases.english: And she gave birth — she (an Israelite) and a priest's woman,
phrases.notes: Standard versions read 'וילדה. ישראלית וכהנת.' The words 'וילדה' also close off the pregnant-convert cases of Step 14.

phrases.english: or she and a Levite's woman,
or she and a woman who had already given birth,
phrases.notes: In each case the babies were mixed up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more cases to the 'for the כהן only' list begun in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed-up babies fall under 'בכור לכהן ואינו בכור לנחלה' because no father can prove which son is his.

steps.title: Widow who remarried too soon, and the ruling for the whole list
steps.stepSummary: A widow who remarried within three months gives birth, and it is unknown whose child it is. This case, like all the cases in the list, is a בכור for the כהן but not for inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, a woman who did not wait three months after her husband and remarried and gave birth. It is unknown if the baby is a nine-month baby of the first husband or a seven-month baby of the second. In all these cases he is a בכור for the כהן but not a בכור for inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the last case of the list, a widow who remarried too soon. Then it states the ruling that covers every case from Step 14 until here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the baby surely opened his mother's womb, so the פדיון obligation stands. But no one knows which husband is the father. So the baby cannot prove he is the firstborn of either one, and cannot collect a double portion from either estate. This is the same reasoning as the mix-up cases: the mother's side is clear, but the father's side is not.

keyTerms.meaning: She waited
Three months (the required waiting period before remarrying)
A baby born after nine months
A baby born after seven months

steps.whatToRemember: Redemption from the כהן depends on the mother ('opening the womb'). Inheritance depends on the father. Whenever the mother's side is clear but the father's side is not (he had sons before, there is no legal father, or the father is unknown), the son is 'בכור לכהן ואינו בכור לנחלה.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why there is a three-month waiting period before a widow or divorcee remarries. Without it, the baby's father cannot be known.

phrases.english: And likewise, a woman who did not wait

and she married and gave birth,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the father is unknown or has no legal tie, the son is redeemed from the כהן but gets no firstborn's double portion.
